_comment: Single source of truth for the winteam-standards size caps. Edited by hand; read by hooks/check_cs_edit.py and hooks/check_comments.py, and applied by /winteam-standards:code-style. The keeping-files-small and keeping-core-methods-small skills restate these values for readability and both say explicitly that this file wins on conflict. If the hook cannot read this file it falls back to the same values hardcoded in the script, so a typo here degrades to defaults rather than breaking the hook.
_maxBodyLinesComment: Target is 10 lines; 15 is where the advisory fires. Method limits apply only under WinTeam.Mobile.Core/ — platform view methods are exempt by design.
_commentCarveOutPrefixesComment: Read by hooks/check_comments.py. An in-body // opening with one of these, or containing a URL, is a marker rather than narration and is never a finding. Set requireDocComments to false to turn off the missing-/// check alone and keep the narration and dead-code checks. Both were counted against the whole repo before shipping, per the rule in README.md: 912 of 948 public members in Core carry no /// block, which is why the check fires only when the declaration line itself changed, and 226 in-body prose comments plus 25 commented-out-code lines, which is why those needed no gate beyond changed lines. Same [] semantics as lengthCarveOuts.
_lengthCarveOutsComment: Exempt from the body-length check only. Their parameter counts are still checked. An explicit [] means no carve-outs and is honoured as written; only a non-list value falls back to the four defaults hardcoded in the hook.
_entityPairCarveOutsComment: Responses that legitimately have no *Entity sibling: write-results and acks. Nothing persists an ack, so there is nothing to cache. Read by the entity-pair checks in hooks/check_cs_edit.py, which would otherwise fire on all nine of these and get the hook muted. A Manager returning one of these directly is the one sanctioned exception to 'no Response above the Manager'. Same [] semantics as lengthCarveOuts.
